editor_note: All three rewritten entries are faithful: entry 3 keeps the caveat that an instance "mehr als ihre zugewiesene Zeit verbrauchen kann, wenn die Zuweisung nicht als Limit festgelegt ist", entry 4 keeps both windows ("rollierendes Zeitfenster von 28 Tagen" for Premium, "Abonnementzeitraum" for Flex), and entry 11 uses the informal du register throughout.

The translation is faithful throughout. The beta caveat and the "0.47.0 oder höher" requirement are kept, and the du-register holds (e.g. "deinen Fehlerminderungs-Workflow", "findest du"). One small inconsistency: [5] renders the noise-learning helper as "Noise-Learning-Hilfsklasse" (correct, since NoiseLearnerV3 is a class), but the guide link title in [10] turns it into "Noise-Learning-Hilfsprogramm", which suggests a separate tool rather than the same helper class. Using one term in both places would fix this.

examples.source: [Noise learning helper](/guides/noise-learning)
examples.translation: [Noise-Learning-Hilfsprogramm](/guides/noise-learning)
examples.suggested: [Noise-Learning-Hilfsklasse](/guides/noise-learning)
examples.why: Entry [5] calls the same helper "Hilfsklasse". "Hilfsprogramm" suggests a standalone program rather than the NoiseLearnerV3 class, so the term is inconsistent within the file.

editor_note: None of the three rewritten entries (8, 14, 21) would mislead a learner. The meaning matches the English: the YGate is added to the target because it is not a basis gate, and the BasisTranslator plus ALAPScheduleAnalysis requirement is kept. Entry 8's "Basis-Gates unseres target" is ungrammatical German: bare lowercase English in a genitive, with no -s and no code formatting. Entry 14 drops the "also" from "This is also why", which loses the link back to entry 9's rationale. It also uses "es" for the feminine "die YGate-Anweisung". Entry 21 is clean.

examples.source: gates that are not necessarily basis gates of our target
examples.translation: Gates umfasst, die nicht notwendigerweise Basis-Gates unseres target sind
examples.suggested: Gates umfasst, die nicht unbedingt Basis-Gates unseres Targets (`target`) sind
examples.why: Bare lowercase English noun in a German genitive, with no case ending, reads as an untranslated leftover. 'notwendigerweise' is also stiffer than 'unbedingt'.

examples.source: This is also why the `basis_gates` were saved separately
examples.translation: Deshalb wurden die `basis_gates` separat gespeichert
examples.suggested: Das ist auch der Grund, warum die `basis_gates` separat gespeichert wurden
examples.why: Dropping 'also' loses the link to the earlier reason given in entry 9 (saving basis_gates before modifying the target). Minor loss of nuance.

examples.source: adding the `YGate` instruction to the `target` although it is not an actual basis gate of `ibm_fez`
examples.translation: da wir die `YGate`-Anweisung zum `target` hinzufügen, obwohl es kein tatsächliches Basis-Gate von `ibm_fez` ist
examples.suggested: da wir die `YGate`-Anweisung zum `target` hinzufügen, obwohl das `YGate` kein echtes Basis-Gate von `ibm_fez` ist
examples.why: The pronoun 'es' does not agree with the feminine antecedent 'Anweisung'. Naming the gate again fixes the reference.

editor_note: Entry 45 leaves out the English opening sentence, "The overhead of this method scales with the number of noise factors." The German keeps only the default-settings example (three noise factors, roughly 3x overhead). A learner therefore misses the general rule that ZNE's cost grows with every noise factor they add, which is the caveat the 3x example is meant to illustrate. Separately, entry 56 renders "twirled" as "getwirten", which looks like a typo for "getwirlten" (from "twirlen"). The remaining 15 delta entries are faithful and read naturally with consistent terms: Fehlerminderung, erwartungstreu for unbiased, Rauschlern-Job, and du-register throughout.

examples.source: The overhead of this method scales with the number of noise factors. The default settings sample the expectation value at three noise factors, leading to a roughly 3x overhead.
examples.translation: Mit den Standardeinstellungen wird der Erwartungswert bei drei Rauschfaktoren abgetastet, was zu einem ungefähr dreifachen Overhead führt.
examples.suggested: Der Overhead dieser Methode skaliert mit der Anzahl der Rauschfaktoren. Mit den Standardeinstellungen wird der Erwartungswert bei drei Rauschfaktoren abgetastet, was zu einem ungefähr dreifachen Overhead führt.
examples.why: The general scaling statement is missing. The learner sees one data point but loses the rule that more noise factors mean proportionally more overhead.

examples.source: learning the twirled noise model of each layer of entangling gates
examples.translation: dem Lernen des getwirten Rauschmodells jeder Schicht von Verschränkungs-Gates
examples.suggested: dem Lernen des getwirlten Rauschmodells jeder Schicht von Verschränkungs-Gates
examples.why: "getwirten" is a malformed participle of "twirlen"; the correct form is "getwirlt".

editor_note: All four rewritten entries (3, 19, 22, 55) keep the meaning of the English, and "mid-circuit measurement" is rendered as "Zwischenmessung" throughout; entry 22 correctly completes the elliptical "optimized for mid-circuit" as "für Zwischenmessungen optimiert", and entry 19 keeps the causal claim "da längere Anweisungen zu stärker verrauschten Circuits führen".

All 7 rewritten entries keep the English meaning. The "only change being the import statement" caveat, the parametrized-circuit condition and the ISA/transpiler instruction are all intact, so nothing here would mislead a learner. A native editor would still fix some phrasing. Entry 4's "Die Schritte in diesem Thema" is a calque of "topic"; "in diesem Leitfaden" would be natural German. Entry 21 treats QPU as masculine ("vom QPU"), but German convention is feminine ("von der QPU", from "Einheit"). Entry 6's "direkte Ersatzlösungen" is stiff for "drop-in replacements".

examples.source: The steps in this topic describe how to set up Estimator
examples.translation: Die Schritte in diesem Thema beschreiben, wie du den Estimator einrichtest
examples.suggested: Dieser Leitfaden beschreibt Schritt für Schritt, wie du den Estimator einrichtest
examples.why: "Thema" is a literal calque of the doc-system term "topic". A German technical writer would say "Leitfaden" or "auf dieser Seite".

examples.source: instructions supported by the QPU
examples.translation: Anweisungen ..., die vom QPU unterstützt werden
examples.suggested: Anweisungen ..., die von der QPU unterstützt werden
examples.why: In German, QPU (Quantum Processing Unit, "Einheit") conventionally takes the feminine article, like CPU/GPU. "vom QPU" reads as an error.

examples.source: largely drop-in replacements of the legacy server-side primitives
examples.translation: größtenteils direkte Ersatzlösungen für die alten serverseitigen Primitives
examples.suggested: können die bisherigen serverseitigen Primitives größtenteils direkt ersetzen
examples.why: "direkte Ersatzlösungen" is stiff translationese. A verbal phrasing reads more naturally and keeps the meaning.

editor_note: None of the 7 rewritten entries changes the meaning. Entry 29 keeps the "nicht sowohl … als auch" mismatch condition exactly, and entry 30 keeps both the silent-accept rule and the QASM2ParseError caveat. The problems are all wording. In entry 51, "quality-of-life improvements" is calqued as "Qualitätsverbesserungen", which makes it sound like the parser output gets better rather than that the parser is more forgiving. "nachfolgende Kommas" is not the usual German term for trailing commas. In entry 55, "einer Legacy-, nicht standardmäßigen Version" is clumsy, and "aber in der Zwischenzeit, wenn du …, verwende …" copies the English sentence order.

examples.source: and several other quality-of-life improvements without emitting any errors
examples.translation: und mehrere andere Qualitätsverbesserungen ohne Ausgabe von Fehlern
examples.suggested: sowie einige weitere Erleichterungen, ohne Fehler auszugeben
examples.why: 'Qualitätsverbesserungen' is a literal calque. 'Quality-of-life' here means convenience or leniency, not quality, so the German suggests something different.

examples.source: It allows trailing commas in parameter lists
examples.translation: Er erlaubt nachfolgende Kommas in Parameterlisten
examples.suggested: Er erlaubt abschließende Kommas in Parameterlisten
examples.why: The usual German term for trailing commas is 'abschließende' (or 'nachgestellte') Kommas. 'nachfolgende' is vague.

examples.source: still assumes a legacy, non-standard version ... but in the meantime, if you need to re-import ..., use ...
examples.translation: geht immer noch von einer Legacy-, nicht standardmäßigen Version ... aus. ... aber in der Zwischenzeit, wenn du ... erneut importieren musst, verwende ...
examples.suggested: geht immer noch von einer veralteten, nicht standardkonformen Version ... aus. ... Bis dahin gilt: Wenn du ... erneut importieren musst, verwende ...
examples.why: The hyphenated 'Legacy-,' adjective is awkward, and the clause order copies the English. A German technical writer would split or reorder the sentence.

editor_note: All seven rewritten entries are faithful and read naturally, with correct and consistent terms: statevector→Zustandsvektor, mixed states→gemischte Zustände, and "Korrelationen zwischen Qubits können nicht dargestellt werden" in [36] keeps the caveat about entanglement.

Both rewritten entries are faithful and read naturally. [8] "mit den folgenden Anforderungen entwickelt … diese Versionen oder neuere" is correct, and [24] keeps the full caveat ("Probleminstanz", "nachfolgenden Verarbeitungsschritten", "klassische und quantengenerierte Stichproben … nach vergleichbarer Nachbearbeitung", "gesamten Optimierungsworkflow").

Of the four rewritten entries, 11 and 49 are faithful and natural ("unter Berücksichtigung des Kontexts", "KI-gestützte Circuit-Optimierung", which matches entry 25). Entry 48 renders "API coverage" as "vollständige API-Dokumentation". That adds a completeness claim the English does not make, and "Dokumentation" now appears twice in one list. Its "Besuche das … für …" frame is also a calque of "Visit … for". Entry 5 turns "detailed API coverage" into "ausführliche API-Dokumentation", which is acceptable but slightly shifts the meaning. Nothing here would mislead a learner in a real way.

examples.source: Visit the [Qiskit MCP Servers GitHub repository](...) for detailed documentation, API coverage, and examples.
examples.translation: Besuche das [Qiskit MCP Servers GitHub-Repository](...) für ausführliche Dokumentation, vollständige API-Dokumentation und Beispiele.
examples.suggested: Ausführliche Dokumentation, eine Übersicht über die API und Beispiele findest du im [Qiskit MCP Servers GitHub-Repository](...).
examples.why: 'vollständige' (complete) is not in the source and overstates a little. 'Dokumentation' is repeated in the same list, and 'Besuche … für …' is calqued from English.

examples.source: For the most up-to-date information, detailed API coverage, and advanced configurations, refer to ...
examples.translation: Die aktuellsten Informationen, eine ausführliche API-Dokumentation und erweiterte Konfigurationen findest du im ...
examples.suggested: Aktuelle Informationen, eine ausführliche Beschreibung der API und erweiterte Konfigurationen findest du im ...
examples.why: 'API coverage' becomes 'API-Dokumentation', which is a small loss of meaning. It is acceptable but not quite faithful.

editor_note: None of the five rewritten entries (7, 26, 27, 54, 57) changes the meaning. Numbers, conditions and the expansion-step logic match the English, and "Einfach- und Zweifachanregungen" and "Dimension des vollständigen aktiven Raums (CAS)" are good choices. Entry 57 has two calques: "Aus den folgenden Benchmark-Ergebnissen konnten wir die chemische Genauigkeit ... mit einer ... Berechnung ... erreichen" is clumsy and wrongly suggests the classical DMRG run was the tool that reached the accuracy, when it is only the comparison reference. Also in entry 57, the relative clause starting with "was" should be "der". In entries 27 and 54, "einen Eigenzustand ... bildet" and "homo-lumo aktive Orbitalauswahl" are stiff, word-for-word renderings.

examples.source: From the following benchmark results, we were able to achieve the chemical accuracy (> 1.6 mHa) with a state-of-the-art classical computer chemistry calculation of CASCI(DMRG) (22o,22e) reference.
examples.translation: Aus den folgenden Benchmark-Ergebnissen konnten wir die chemische Genauigkeit (> 1,6 mHa) mit einer hochmodernen klassischen Computerchemie-Berechnung der CASCI(DMRG) (22o,22e)-Referenz erreichen.
examples.suggested: Wie die folgenden Benchmark-Ergebnisse zeigen, erreichen wir chemische Genauigkeit (> 1,6 mHa) gegenüber einer hochmodernen klassischen CASCI(DMRG)-Referenzrechnung (22o,22e).
examples.why: The 'Aus den ... Ergebnissen konnten wir' construction is a calque. 'mit einer ... Berechnung erreichen' makes it sound as if the classical calculation produced the accuracy, but it is only the comparison reference.

examples.source: ...(NO) ligand, which represents a biologically relevant metalloporphyrin system that plays crucial roles...
examples.translation: ...Stickstoffmonoxid-Liganden (NO), was ein biologisch relevantes Metalloporphyrinsystem darstellt und ... eine entscheidende Rolle spielt.
examples.suggested: ...Stickstoffmonoxid-Liganden (NO) – ein biologisch relevantes Metalloporphyrinsystem, das in verschiedenen physiologischen Prozessen eine entscheidende Rolle spielt.
examples.why: The relative pronoun 'was' refers to a whole clause, but the antecedent here is the complex. It reads awkwardly.

examples.source: whether the computed state forms an eigenstate of the system's Hamiltonian
examples.translation: ob der berechnete Zustand einen Eigenzustand des Hamiltonoperators des Systems bildet
examples.suggested: ob der berechnete Zustand ein Eigenzustand des Hamiltonoperators des Systems ist
examples.why: 'einen Eigenzustand bilden' is a word-for-word copy of 'forms'. German physics writing says 'ein Eigenzustand sein'.

editor_note: All four rewritten entries (23, 25, 27, 46) keep the English meaning, and none would mislead a learner. Entry 25 keeps the directional-graph caveat and the SWAP-routing claim intact. Entry 23 keeps "in der Regel" and uses "den/der QPU" consistently with the rest of the page. The one issue is in entry 27: the parenthetical "— die die tatsächlichen Qubits auswählt —" sits after "verzahnt ist", away from "_Layout_-Phase". Because both phases are feminine, "die" could refer to either one, so a native editor would move the clause next to "Layout-Phase". Entry 46 drops the redundant "as the target", which is fine.

examples.source: Although the routing stage is intertwined with the _layout_ stage — which selects the actual qubits — by default, this topic treats them as separate stages for simplicity.
examples.translation: Obwohl die Routing-Phase standardmäßig mit der _Layout_-Phase verzahnt ist — die die tatsächlichen Qubits auswählt — behandelt dieses Thema sie der Einfachheit halber als separate Phasen.
examples.suggested: Obwohl die Routing-Phase standardmäßig mit der _Layout_-Phase (die die tatsächlichen Qubits auswählt) verzahnt ist, behandelt dieses Thema beide der Einfachheit halber als separate Phasen.
examples.why: The relative clause comes after the verb, away from its antecedent. Since both phases are feminine, 'die' could refer to either the routing or the layout phase, and the dash-clause-dash layout copies the English word order stiffly.

editor_note: The meaning in all four rewritten entries (0, 6, 10, 12) matches the English. The noise caveat, the point that reference primitives do not model noise, and the exact versus noisy expectation-value framing all come through. The problems are in German word formation. Entry 10 writes "den Estimator Primitive", which treats the English singular as a masculine noun, while entry 6 declines the word as German ("Referenz-Primitive", "Primitiven"). The German singular should be "das Estimator-Primitiv". Entries 0 and 6 also leave compounds open that German hyphenates: "Qiskit Aer Primitiven" should be "Qiskit-Aer-Primitiven" and "Quantum Circuit Simulator" should be hyphenated.

examples.source: use the Estimator primitive from Qiskit Aer
examples.translation: verwenden den Estimator Primitive von Qiskit Aer
examples.suggested: verwenden das Estimator-Primitiv von Qiskit Aer
examples.why: This uses the English singular with masculine gender. Entry 6 declines 'Primitiv' as a German noun, so the file is inconsistent. The German singular is 'das Primitiv', joined to 'Estimator' with a hyphen.

examples.source: with Qiskit Aer primitives
examples.translation: mit Qiskit Aer Primitiven
examples.suggested: mit Qiskit-Aer-Primitiven
examples.why: German writes multi-part compounds with hyphens. Leaving them open reads like an English calque. The same problem appears in entry 6 ('Qiskit Aer Primitiven', 'Quantum Circuit Simulator').

editor_note: All 7 rewritten entries say what the English says, so none would mislead a learner. The orchestra analogy (Dirigent / Instrumentengruppen / Musiker) and the claim that higher optimization levels trade quality for transpilation time both come through intact. Three small polish issues remain. Entry 12 writes "Basisgatter (Basis-Gates)" with a doubled gloss, while every other entry in the file uses "Gates" (entries 15, 17 and 18). Entry 18's "Basissatz von Anweisungen" is a calque, and entry 27 opens with a German „ but closes with a straight ASCII quote.

examples.source: such as the hardware's available basis gates
examples.translation: wie die verfügbaren Basisgatter (Basis-Gates) der Hardware
examples.suggested: wie die verfügbaren Basis-Gates der Hardware
examples.why: The doubled gloss is clunky, and 'Gatter' clashes with the 'Gates' used in every other entry on the page.

examples.source: translates the gates in the circuit to the QPU's basis set of instructions
examples.translation: übersetzt die Gates im Schaltkreis in den Basissatz von Anweisungen der QPU
examples.suggested: übersetzt die Gates im Schaltkreis in den Basis-Befehlssatz der QPU
examples.why: 'Basissatz von Anweisungen' copies the English structure word for word. 'Basis-Befehlssatz' is the idiomatic German compound.

examples.line_approx: Für einen einfacheren, aber weniger anpassbaren …
examples.source: "out-of-the-box" way
examples.translation: „Out-of-the-Box"-Ansatz
examples.suggested: „Out-of-the-Box“-Ansatz
examples.why: The German opening quote „ is closed with a straight ASCII quote instead of the matching “.

editor_note: None of the 7 rewritten entries would mislead a learner. The 3/4 classical bound, the optimality claim for Tsirelson's inequality and the 2022 Nobel attribution all carry over correctly. The image alt texts in entries 136, 139 and 143 all say "Fall 1", but that repeats the English source, so they are faithful. Two small wording issues remain. In entry 17, "denn es gibt" turns the English "and" into a cause-and-effect link, and "sehr interessant" makes the source's plain "also interesting" a bit stronger. In entry 150, "eine hohe Sicherheit, dass" is a calque of "a high degree of confidence"; "großes Vertrauen darin, dass" would read more naturally.

examples.source: It's extremely interesting, in fact, and there are some nonlocal games for which it's currently not known how well Alice and Bob can play using entanglement.
examples.translation: Das ist in der Tat äußerst spannend, denn es gibt nichtlokale Spiele, für die bisher nicht bekannt ist, wie gut Alice und Bob mit Quantenverschränkung abschneiden können.
examples.suggested: Tatsächlich ist das äußerst spannend, und es gibt nichtlokale Spiele, für die bisher nicht bekannt ist, wie gut Alice und Bob mit Verschränkung abschneiden können.
examples.why: "denn" adds a causal link the English does not make, and "Quantenverschränkung" does not match the plain "Verschränkung" used everywhere else in the file. Neither changes the meaning.

examples.source: This provides us with a high degree of confidence that entanglement is real
examples.translation: Das gibt uns eine hohe Sicherheit, dass Verschränkung real ist
examples.suggested: Das gibt uns großes Vertrauen darin, dass Verschränkung real ist
examples.why: "eine hohe Sicherheit, dass" is a calque of the English phrase. A native technical writer would use "großes Vertrauen darin" or "ein hohes Maß an Gewissheit".

editor_note: None of the five rewritten entries would mislead a learner. The case analysis in [22]–[25] keeps every cd value, Bell state, target state and the −1 phase caveat intact. In [4], "less interesting" became "weniger beeindruckend", so the page's point that the feat is less interesting but still not uninteresting ("uninteressant") loses its echo; "weniger interessant" would restore it. In [22]–[25], "transformiert diesen Zustand zu |00⟩" is a calque of "transforms into"; a native German editor would write "überführt diesen Zustand in".

examples.source: It is reasonable to view this feat as being less interesting than the one that teleportation accomplishes.
examples.translation: Man könnte diese Leistung als weniger beeindruckend als die der Teleportation betrachten.
examples.suggested: Man kann diese Leistung durchaus als weniger interessant ansehen als die der Teleportation.
examples.why: 'interesting' shifted to 'beeindruckend', which breaks the echo with 'uninteressant' in the last sentence. The English deliberately contrasts 'less interesting' with 'not uninteresting'.

examples.source: He transforms this state into $\vert 00\rangle$ and obtains $cd = 00$.
examples.translation: Er transformiert diesen Zustand zu $\vert 00\rangle$ und erhält $cd = 00$.
examples.suggested: Er überführt diesen Zustand in $\vert 00\rangle$ und erhält $cd = 00$.
examples.why: 'transformiert ... zu' is a calque. The idiomatic German is 'überführt ... in' (or 'transformiert ... in'). The same wording appears in [23]–[25].

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout: 20 questions, a pass mark of 16, two attempts before the lock, and the Credly data-sharing notice all match the source. There are two small editorial slips. In [8], "Nach Erreichen einer Bestehensgrenze" is a stiff calque of "upon receiving a passing score" (you do not "reach a threshold" as an event), and "Sobald du bestanden hast" is the natural phrasing. The course title is also handled inconsistently: [5] keeps the English "Basics of Quantum Information" in straight quotes, while [7] translates it as „Grundlagen der Quanteninformation" and pairs a German opening quote with a straight closing quote.

examples.source: Upon receiving a passing score, your badge will automatically be sent to the email you used to register
examples.translation: Nach Erreichen einer Bestehensgrenze wird dein Badge automatisch an die E-Mail-Adresse geschickt
examples.suggested: Sobald du bestanden hast, wird dein Badge automatisch an die E-Mail-Adresse geschickt
examples.why: 'Erreichen einer Bestehensgrenze' is an unidiomatic calque. A native writer would say you have passed the exam, not that you reached a threshold.

examples.source: Congratulations on completing the "Basics of Quantum Information" course by IBM!
examples.translation: Herzlichen Glückwunsch zum Abschluss des Kurses "Basics of Quantum Information" von IBM!
examples.suggested: Herzlichen Glückwunsch zum Abschluss des Kurses „Grundlagen der Quanteninformation“ von IBM!
examples.why: The course title stays in English here but is translated in [1] and [7]. The quotation marks are also inconsistent: straight quotes here, and in [7] a German opening quote with a straight closing quote.

editor_note: I checked all 10 rewritten entries against the English and none of them misleads a learner. The quantities (2^r, 4^{n-r}, d/2), the n=r caveat and the weight argument in entries 152 and 159 all come through correctly. Three spots read stiffly. In entry 147, "tie for the lowest weight" became "für den niedrigstgewichtigen Fehler … gleichwertig". That is clumsy, and "gleichwertig" sits close to the "äquivalent" error classes introduced just before it. Entry 145 stacks two relative clauses ("Klassen von Pauli-Operationen, die als Fehler betrachtet werden, die mit jedem möglichen Syndrom konsistent sind"). In entry 93, "Insbesondere gilt dies einfach für Hadamard-Gates" reads as "this simply holds" rather than "this is easy for Hadamard gates".

examples.source: There may in fact be multiple operations that tie for the lowest weight error consistent with a given syndrome, in which case any one of them may be selected.
examples.translation: Es kann tatsächlich mehrere Operationen geben, die für den niedrigstgewichtigen Fehler zu einem gegebenen Syndrom gleichwertig sind – in diesem Fall kann eine beliebige davon gewählt werden.
examples.suggested: Es kann tatsächlich mehrere Operationen mit demselben minimalen Gewicht geben, die zum gegebenen Syndrom passen – in diesem Fall kann eine beliebige davon gewählt werden.
examples.why: The German does not express 'tie' naturally. Also, 'gleichwertig' is easy to confuse with the equivalence classes of errors defined in entries 144 and 145.

examples.source: This leaves $4^{n-r}$ inequivalent classes of Pauli operations, considered as errors, that are consistent with each possible syndrome.
examples.translation: Das lässt $4^{n-r}$ inäquivalente Klassen von Pauli-Operationen, die als Fehler betrachtet werden, die mit jedem möglichen Syndrom konsistent sind.
examples.suggested: Damit bleiben für jedes mögliche Syndrom $4^{n-r}$ inäquivalente Klassen von Pauli-Fehlern, die mit ihm konsistent sind.
examples.why: The two stacked relative clauses copy the English sentence structure word for word and read like machine translation.

examples.source: In particular, this is easy for Hadamard gates,
examples.translation: Insbesondere gilt dies einfach für Hadamard-Gates:
examples.suggested: Für Hadamard-Gates ist das besonders einfach:
examples.why: 'gilt dies einfach' reads as 'this simply holds' instead of 'this is easy to check'.

editor_note: None of the three rewritten entries (50, 70, 115) would mislead a learner. The meaning matches the English, including the GGT caveat, the "base 2 analogue" of school addition, and the reserved use of "subexponentiell". A native editor would still fix a few small things. In entry 115, "im Exponenten nur mit dem Exponenten 1/3" repeats "Exponent" awkwardly. Entry 70 mixes an em dash (—) with an en dash (–) in one sentence, and "dem Verfahren entspricht, wie" is a little clumsy. Entry 50 drops "as we go along" ("im weiteren Verlauf"), and "außer einigen interessanten Fakten dazu" reads as elliptical.

examples.source: because $n$ is raised to the power $1/3$ in the exponent
examples.translation: weil $n$ im Exponenten nur mit dem Exponenten $1/3$ auftritt
examples.suggested: weil $n$ im Exponenten nur in der Potenz $1/3$ auftritt
examples.why: Repeating 'Exponent' in one clause sounds clumsy; 'in der Potenz' says the same thing more cleanly.

examples.source: which is the base $2$ analogue to the way addition is taught in elementary/primary schools around the world
examples.translation: — der dem Verfahren entspricht, wie Addition weltweit in der Grundschule gelehrt wird – nur zur Basis $2$.
examples.suggested: – der das Gegenstück zur Basis $2$ zu dem Verfahren ist, mit dem Addition weltweit in der Grundschule gelehrt wird.
examples.why: One sentence uses both an em dash and an en dash, and 'dem Verfahren entspricht, wie' is awkward German. The meaning is kept.

examples.source: aside from including a few interesting facts concerning circuit depth as we go along
examples.translation: außer einigen interessanten Fakten dazu
examples.suggested: abgesehen von einigen interessanten Fakten zur Schaltkreistiefe, die wir im weiteren Verlauf einstreuen
examples.why: The German drops 'as we go along' and reads as elliptical. The loss is minor and does not mislead.

editor_note: All three rewritten entries match their English and read natively: [21] renders "partly distributed (leaving the states of qubit 1 factored out)" correctly as "teilweise ausmultipliziert … ausgeklammert", [51] keeps the scalar-through-tensor-product reasoning intact ("Skalare frei durch Tensorprodukte hindurchwandern"), and [58] uses "Quantencircuit"/"Abfrage-Gate" consistently with the rest of the page.

The translation is faithful, natural and uses informal "du" consistently. The exam rules keep the source meaning: "mindestens 16 davon richtig beantworten" and "in zwei Versuchen kein ausreichendes Ergebnis … vorübergehend gesperrt". The Credly privacy notice is rendered accurately and cleanly.

None of the 7 rewritten entries would mislead a learner. Entry 15's caveat ("können immer noch ... erreicht werden – aber er übertraf Brute-Force-Algorithmen") and entry 40's hedging are carried over faithfully. The problems are calques. Entry 18 renders "This is where IBM has chosen to focus" as a place ("Hier hat IBM beschlossen, sich zu konzentrieren") and uses the stiff "um Quantenrechnerleistung zu suchen". Entry 48 opens with "Eine Möglichkeit, darüber nachzudenken, ist durch eine Analogie" and has computers "handeln" in accordance with laws. Entry 52 drops "or research facility" from the basement-lab aside, keeping only "Universitätskellerlabor", and entry 65 uses "interferieren" for crosstalk, a word with a specific quantum meaning, where "sich stören" fits better.

examples.source: This is where IBM has chosen to focus — to look for quantum computational power and reach toward an eventual quantum advantage.
examples.translation: Hier hat IBM beschlossen, sich zu konzentrieren – um Quantenrechnerleistung zu suchen und auf einen letztendlichen Quantum Advantage hinzuarbeiten.
examples.suggested: Genau darauf konzentriert sich IBM – um nach Quantenrechenleistung zu suchen und letztlich auf einen Quantum Advantage hinzuarbeiten.
examples.why: 'Hier ... sich zu konzentrieren' is a word-for-word copy of the English 'this is where'. 'Quantenrechnerleistung zu suchen' and 'letztendlichen' are stiff.

examples.source: One way to think about this is through an analogy to wind tunnels. ... because they act in accordance with those laws
examples.translation: Eine Möglichkeit, darüber nachzudenken, ist durch eine Analogie zu Windkanälen. ... da sie in Übereinstimmung mit diesen Gesetzen handeln
examples.suggested: Eine hilfreiche Analogie ist der Windkanal. ... da sie selbst diesen Gesetzen folgen
examples.why: 'ist durch eine Analogie' copies the English sentence structure. 'handeln' suggests the computer acts on purpose, and 'Tunnel mit blasendem Wind' is also stiff.

examples.source: (usually in a sad, basement lab in a university or research facility)
examples.translation: (normalerweise in einem trüben Universitätskellerlabor)
examples.suggested: (meist in einem tristen Kellerlabor einer Universität oder Forschungseinrichtung)
examples.why: 'or research facility' is dropped, so the aside now names only universities. The opening 'Bis vor Kurzem, wenn du ... wolltest, musstest du' also follows English clause order.

examples.source: good quality qubits that don't interfere with one another through crosstalk
examples.translation: Qubits, die nicht durch Übersprechen miteinander interferieren
examples.suggested: Qubits, die sich nicht durch Übersprechen gegenseitig stören
examples.why: 'interferieren' has a specific quantum meaning (interference), which is not what crosstalk is. 'sich stören' is the normal wording here.

editor_note: Both rewritten entries match their English: [68] keeps the tradeoff ("Näherungslösungen statt der optimalen Lösung", "konvergiert QAOA gegen den QAA-Fall ... rechnerisch sehr aufwändig"), and [78] renders "native" as „nativer“ Ein- und Zwei-Qubit-Gates, keeps ISA and uses the page's du-form "denk daran".

The meaning is faithful throughout: the 20 questions, the 16 needed to pass, the two-attempt lockout and the maintenance notice all match the source, and the du register holds. A native editor would still change three things. "bestandene Punktzahl" in [8] and [9] is a calque of "passing score" and should read "wenn du die Prüfung bestehst". "des Badge" / "deines Badge" in [12] is missing its genitive -s. [12] also renders "third-party data processor" as just "Drittanbieter", which drops the data-processor role (Auftragsverarbeiter).

examples.source: Upon receiving a passing score, your badge will automatically be sent
examples.translation: Wenn du eine bestandene Punktzahl erreichst, wird dein Badge automatisch ... geschickt
examples.suggested: Wenn du die Prüfung bestehst, wird dein Badge automatisch ... geschickt
examples.why: "bestandene Punktzahl" is a literal calque: a score is not "bestanden", only the exam is. The same wording appears again in [9] ("keine bestandene Punktzahl erreichst" → "die Prüfung nicht bestehst").

examples.source: instructions for claiming the badge ... used to issue your badge
examples.translation: Anweisungen zur Einlösung des Badge ... zur Ausstellung deines Badge
examples.suggested: Anweisungen zur Einlösung des Badges ... zur Ausstellung deines Badges
examples.why: The genitive -s is missing on the neuter loanword "Badge".

examples.source: Credly, a third-party data processor authorized by IBM
examples.translation: Credly, einem von IBM autorisierten Drittanbieter
examples.suggested: Credly, einem von IBM beauftragten externen Auftragsverarbeiter
examples.why: "data processor" is a legal privacy term (Auftragsverarbeiter under GDPR). "Drittanbieter" drops that role, so the qualifier is lost.

editor_note: Nothing here would mislead a learner. The overview and exam entries are faithful, use "du" throughout and read naturally ("damit du so schnell wie möglich loslegen kannst"). A native editor would still fix three small things in the Credly notice [12]. "IBM Digital Badge-Programms" is a hyphenation error and should be "IBM-Digital-Badge-Programms". "third-party data processor" is shortened to "Drittanbieter", which loses the data-processor role (in German, "Auftragsverarbeiter"). "erreichtes Badge" is an odd collocation where "erworbenes Badge" is normal.

examples.source: to assist in the administration of the IBM Digital Badge program
examples.translation: um die Verwaltung des IBM Digital Badge-Programms zu unterstützen
examples.suggested: um die Verwaltung des IBM-Digital-Badge-Programms zu unterstützen
examples.why: German compounds built on a multi-word proper name need hyphens between all parts (Durchkopplung). A hyphen only before 'Programms' is an orthography error.

examples.source: Credly, a third-party data processor authorized by IBM
examples.translation: Credly, einem von IBM autorisierten Drittanbieter
examples.suggested: Credly, einem von IBM beauftragten externen Auftragsverarbeiter
examples.why: The source says Credly processes data for IBM. 'Drittanbieter' drops that role, which is the legally relevant part of a privacy notice.

examples.source: (name, email address, and badge earned)
examples.translation: (Name, E-Mail-Adresse und erreichtes Badge)
examples.suggested: (Name, E-Mail-Adresse und erworbenes Badge)
examples.why: In German you 'erwerben' a badge; 'erreichen' sounds unnatural with 'Badge'.

editor_note: The page has only four short prose entries. All of them are faithful: nothing drifts in meaning and "Klassische Simulation" is used consistently. The one issue is in entry [3], where "wird aber sehr empfohlen" is a stiff calque of "highly recommended". A native editor would write "wird aber dringend empfohlen" or "ist aber sehr zu empfehlen".

examples.source: This lesson can be considered optional, but is highly recommended.
examples.translation: Diese Lektion gilt als optional, wird aber sehr empfohlen.
examples.suggested: Diese Lektion ist optional, wird aber dringend empfohlen.
examples.why: In German, "sehr" does not idiomatically modify "empfohlen" in the passive. "dringend empfohlen" is the standard phrase.

editor_note: None of the six rewritten entries would mislead a learner. The qubit-flip frequencies (28, 35), the 5/16 and 10/16 rotation example (34) and the division by 2^n (98) all match the English. Entry 79 has two naturalness problems: "das gesteuerte Unitäre $CU$" uses an adjective as a noun, which is awkward (better: "die kontrollierte unitäre Operation $CU$"), and "anwendet, nur wenn" copies English word order (better: "nur dann anwendet, wenn"). Entry 25 has "eine in Binär kodierte Zahl", which should be "binär kodierte Zahl", and "Du erinnerst dich sicher" sounds a little more certain than "You likely recall".

examples.source: We need to introduce the controlled unitary $CU$ that applies the unitary operator $U$ on the target register only if its corresponding control bit is $|1\rangle$.
examples.translation: Wir führen das gesteuerte Unitäre $CU$ ein, das den unitären Operator $U$ auf das Zielregister anwendet, nur wenn das entsprechende Steuer-Bit $|1\rangle$ ist.
examples.suggested: Wir führen die kontrollierte unitäre Operation $CU$ ein, die den unitären Operator $U$ nur dann auf das Zielregister anwendet, wenn das zugehörige Kontrollbit $|1\rangle$ ist.
examples.why: 'das gesteuerte Unitäre' uses an adjective as a noun, which is awkward, and 'anwendet, nur wenn' follows English word order; German uses 'nur dann …, wenn'.

examples.source: consider the stepped images below which show a number encoded in binary, using four qubits
examples.translation: betrachte die schrittweisen Bilder unten, die eine in Binär kodierte Zahl mit vier Qubits zeigen
examples.suggested: betrachte die folgenden Einzelbilder, die eine mit vier Qubits binär kodierte Zahl zeigen
examples.why: 'in Binär kodiert' is not idiomatic German; the usual phrasing is 'binär kodiert' or 'in Binärdarstellung'.

examples.source: You likely recall that the Fourier transform ...
examples.translation: Du erinnerst dich sicher, dass die Fourier-Transformation ...
examples.suggested: Du erinnerst dich wahrscheinlich, dass die Fourier-Transformation ...
examples.why: 'sicher' is slightly more certain than 'likely'. This is a small change in tone, not in meaning.

editor_note: None of the three rewritten entries (19, 59, 61) changes the meaning. The figures (24 %, 36 %, 100+ Qubits, under 1 %, about 10.000 gates, depth over 1.000), SABRE's gate-count advantage and the mirror-circuit caveat all match the English. The only thing a native editor would fix is in entry 61's first sentence. It keeps the English word order ("weit unter 1 % in diesem Maßstab"), and "was kaum ein nutzbares Signal lässt" drops the "übrig" that German needs there. Entries 19 and 59 read naturally, and their terms (Zwei-Qubit-Gate-Anzahl, Schaltungstiefe, Heavy-Hex-Topologie, durchweg) match the rest of the file.

examples.source: Both methods produce survival probabilities well under 1% at this scale, leaving little usable signal.
examples.translation: Beide Methoden erzeugen Überlebenswahrscheinlichkeiten weit unter 1 % in diesem Maßstab, was kaum ein nutzbares Signal lässt.
examples.suggested: In diesem Maßstab liefern beide Methoden Überlebenswahrscheinlichkeiten weit unter 1 %, sodass kaum ein nutzbares Signal übrig bleibt.
examples.why: The adverbial phrase sits where the English puts it, which is unidiomatic in German, and 'lässt' without 'übrig' is incomplete. The meaning is still correct.

editor_note: The four rewritten entries are faithful and read naturally. "cutting gates resulting in swap gates" becomes "Gates schneiden, die sonst Swap-Gates nach sich ziehen würden", which states the intended meaning correctly, and "Quasiwahrscheinlichkeitsverteilungen" in [30]/[33] matches entry [23].

None of the five rewritten entries (16, 38, 49, 57, 76) would mislead a learner. The angle bound caveat ("innerhalb bestimmter Grenzen"), the Qiskit v2.4.1 limitation, and the FoldRzzAngle behaviour (negative RZZ values folded to positive, extra X gates added) all match the English. The one thing a native editor would change is in entry 16: it uses the bare anglicism "Unitaries", where German technical prose normally says "unitäre Operationen". Two other choices are fine and should stay. "Anforderungen" in [38] keeps "Requirements" distinct from "Voraussetzungen" in [10]. "Standard-Qiskit-Patterns-Workflow" in [57] matches the rest of the file.

examples.source: you can implement certain unitaries more efficiently on hardware.

examples.suggested: lassen sich bestimmte unitäre Operationen effizienter auf der Hardware implementieren.

editor_note: Entry [1] keeps the OpenInLabBanner attributes the same and translates only the description, faithfully: "Dieses Tutorial wurde für doQumentation erstellt."

Nothing in the 8 rewritten entries would mislead a learner. All the numbers, comparisons and caveats in 118–121 match the English, including "worst estimator", the k = 6 caveat, the t/k_min ≤ 1 rule and the ordering-can-shift note. Entry 65 has two small slips. Its heading says "Hamiltonian-Simulation", but the page already uses "Hamiltonsche Simulation" (entries 6 and 11). It also says "Tensor-Netzwerk-Simulation der späteren dynamischen Koeffizienten" ("simulation of the later dynamic coefficients"), when the English means a tensor-network simulation used later to compute the dynamic coefficients.

examples.source: **Gate collection at the Hamiltonian-simulation level.**
examples.translation: **Gate-Sammlung auf Ebene der Hamiltonian-Simulation.**
examples.suggested: **Gate-Sammlung auf Ebene der Hamiltonschen Simulation.**
examples.why: The page already says "Hamiltonsche Simulation" in entries 6 and 11. This mixed English–German compound breaks that consistency.

examples.source: more amenable to tensor-network simulation for the dynamic-coefficient computation later
examples.translation: die sich besser für die Tensor-Netzwerk-Simulation der späteren dynamischen Koeffizienten eignet
examples.suggested: die sich besser für die Tensor-Netzwerk-Simulation eignet, mit der später die dynamischen Koeffizienten berechnet werden
examples.why: The German reads as if the coefficients themselves are being simulated. In the English, the simulation is the tool used to compute them.

editor_note: Nothing here would mislead a learner. The physics prose is faithful: frustration, extensive energy, the variance scaling and NP-hard all come through correctly, and the terms are consistent (Hamiltonoperator, Schaltkreis, Kopplungsstärke, transpiliert). A native editor would still fix three small things. [11] copies the English comma into „zerklüfteten“, Energielandschaft, where German takes none. [27] drops "to your local environment". [37] "Verwende optional options" reads as an untranslated fragment, so the parameter name needs code formatting or a German noun. The register is informal du throughout.

examples.source: a highly complex, "rugged", energy landscape
examples.translation: einer hochkomplexen, „zerklüfteten“, Energielandschaft
examples.suggested: einer hochkomplexen, „zerklüfteten“ Energielandschaft
examples.why: The comma before the noun is copied from the English. In German it is wrong between an attribute and its noun.

examples.source: you've already saved your account to your local environment
examples.translation: dass du dein Konto bereits gespeichert hast
examples.suggested: dass du dein Konto bereits in deiner lokalen Umgebung gespeichert hast
examples.why: The qualifier about where the account is saved (locally) was dropped. It is a small loss of setup context.

examples.source: Optionally, use options for additional control over the submission:

editor_note: None of the five rewritten entries (20, 21, 29, 33, 74) would mislead a learner; the meaning in each matches the English. Entry 74 has a formatting slip: the compound "Pauli-Twirl-Rauschmodells" is split across a source line break after the hyphen. Markdown turns that break into a space, so the page shows "Pauli-Twirl- Rauschmodells", which looks like a dangling suspended hyphen. Entry 29 uses the half-English "Stretch-Faktoren", while the table in entry 27 already uses German "Puls-Dehnung"; "Streckfaktoren" would read more naturally, though the term is still recognizable.

examples.source:
after learning the Pauli-twirled
noise model for layers of twirled two-qubit basis gates
examples.translation:
nach dem Erlernen des Pauli-Twirl-
Rauschmodells für Twirl-Schichten von Zwei-Qubit-Basis-Gates
examples.suggested: nach dem Erlernen des Pauli-Twirl-Rauschmodells für Twirl-Schichten von Zwei-Qubit-Basis-Gates (keep the compound on one line)

examples.suggested: Gate-Faltung erfordert große Streckfaktoren, die die Tiefe der ausführbaren Circuits stark einschränken.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout. The overhead numbers (γ²=100 vs ≈6.3, about 16x), the postselection formula, the "both qubits on an edge" discard rule and the convergence claims all match the English. A few renderings would still get changed by a native editor. "stem plot" is calqued as "Stammdiagramm" (should be Stabdiagramm or Stem-Plot). Lattice "site" appears as "Stelle" in [13] but as "standortgemittelt" in [46], which suggests a geographic location. "fidelity" is flattened to "Genauigkeit" in [17], and "mediator qubits measuring |1⟩" is calqued as "Qubits, die |1⟩ messen", which makes the qubits the ones doing the measuring.

examples.source: The stem plot below the QPU noise map
examples.translation: Das Stammdiagramm unter der QPU-Rauschkarte
examples.suggested: Das Stabdiagramm (Stem-Plot) unter der QPU-Rauschkarte
examples.why: 'Stammdiagramm' is a literal calque, not a German name for a chart type.

examples.source: site-averaged ⟨X⟩
examples.translation: des standortgemittelten ⟨X⟩
examples.suggested: des über alle Gitterplätze gemittelten ⟨X⟩
examples.why: 'Standort' means a geographic location. In an Ising lattice, 'site' is 'Gitterplatz', and [13] used 'Stelle' for the same term, so the file is inconsistent.

examples.source: One or more mediator qubits measuring |1⟩ indicates ... can improve the fidelity of the sampled distribution.
examples.translation: Ein oder mehrere Mediator-Qubits, die |1⟩ messen, zeigen an ... kann die Genauigkeit der gesampelten Verteilung verbessern.
examples.suggested: Wird an einem oder mehreren Mediator-Qubits |1⟩ gemessen, zeigt dies an ... kann die Fidelität der gesampelten Verteilung verbessern.
examples.why: The German makes the qubits the ones measuring, which is a calque. 'Fidelity' is a technical term in this field, and 'Genauigkeit' is a flattened rendering of it.

examples.source: the structure of a boxed circuit
examples.translation: die Struktur eines eingerahmten Schaltkreises
examples.suggested: die Struktur eines in Boxen gruppierten Schaltkreises

editor_note: None of the 7 rewritten entries changes the meaning. The 127+ qubit backend in [35], the 100-node weighted graph in [64], the objective/constraints caveat in [15] ("Nebenbedingungen") and COBYLA's noise limitation in [51] all match the English. Two wording slips remain. In [51], "random jitter" becomes "zufälligem Rauschen", so the sentence says "Rauschen" twice and the difference between hardware noise and step-to-step jitter is lost. "zufälligen Schwankungen" would keep them apart. In [64], "ein Problem im „Utility-Scale“" is stiff, and entry [27] already uses the more natural compound "Utility-Scale-Problem".

examples.source: its linear-approximation model can no longer tell real descent from random jitter

examples.why: 'Rauschen' already stands for noise in the same sentence. Using it again for 'jitter' repeats the word and blurs two separate ideas: the noise itself and the step-to-step fluctuations it causes.

editor_note: None of the five rewritten entries (17, 18, 45, 47, 55) would mislead a learner. The scaling argument in [47], the kernel-trick explanation in [18] and the row 15, column 20 placement in [45] all match the English. There are three small polish issues. In [18], "in Termen der ursprünglichen Datenvektoren geschrieben" is a calque of the English "in terms of". Also, [17] and [18] mix "Kernel" and "Kern" in parallel compounds ("Kernel-Methoden" vs "Quantenkern-Methoden", "Kernel" vs "Kernmatrix"/"Kernfunktion"). examples.suggested: durch die ursprünglichen Datenvektoren ausgedrückt werden kann

examples.source: Kernel methods ... Quantum kernel methods

examples.suggested: Kernel-Methoden ... Quantenkernel-Methoden (or Kern-Methoden ... Quantenkern-Methoden)

editor_note: None of the 8 rewritten entries changes the meaning. Entry 15 correctly takes the subspace to be spanned by the samples, and entry 60 keeps the "obwohl" caveat and the error condition. There are three small editorial fixes. Entry 51 copies English word order in "der spezialisiert ist auf die Transpilierung …" (German puts the verb last). examples.suggested: um einen Pass-Manager zu erstellen, der auf die Transpilierung des LUCJ-Ansatzes für das gegebene Backend spezialisiert ist

editor_note: None of the seven rewritten entries misleads the reader. The numbers all match the English: 3+2 steps compressed out of 10, 6+4 out of 20, max_bond 32 and 128, and a cap of 100 L-BFGS-B iterations. "bond dimension" becomes "MPS-Bindungsdimension" in entries 46, 54 and 59, where German physics texts normally say "Bonddimension". editor_note: Both rewritten entries are faithful and read naturally: [50] keeps the 2 × maxiter call count and renders "can be increased to any higher value" as "lässt sich beliebig erhöhen", and [67] keeps the SQD description intact ("projiziert den Hamiltonian auf einen Unterraum, der von diesen Samples aufgespannt wird", "obere Schranke für die Grundzustandsenergie"), using the same "Hamiltonian" and "Barren-Plateaus" terms as the rest of the file.
